Finding: The site: operator failed at all ten institutions (0 to 2 on-domain hits per seven searches), with domain collisions at short domains (hsu.edu to hsu.edu.hk, fhsu.edu; umgc.edu to UMBC, UMD).
Protocol change: Replace site: searches with the search tool's domain filter, plus a seventh unrestricted string pairing the institution name with "artificial intelligence". Product-name strings (Gemini, Copilot) outperformed policy-vocabulary strings.

Finding: Nearly every document was reached by link-following from office pages, with the IT division's AI hub the most frequent entry point (Jackson State, Morgan State, Worcester State, Texas State).
Protocol change: Step 3 adds an institutional AI hub or landing page, the online education unit, and the current catalog.

Finding: Catalog-hosted policies sit on vendor domains (cleancatalog.io, Acalog, smartcatalogiq) outside the primary domain, and Acalog rate-limits and blocks search.
Protocol change: Mandatory catalog walk per institution, spaced single fetches for Acalog.

Finding: System documents are hosted on component file servers (TSUS on docs.gato.txst.edu) or distributed by campus offices (UPR Cert. 66 at the Procuraduría), and campus-level search finds system documents by leak.
Protocol change: Read issuing office from the document, never from the hosting domain. Record whether the campus links to the system document.

Finding: Long PDFs (handbooks, catalogs, employee handbooks) exceed the fetch extraction limit, so policies at high page numbers (WWU p.123, MSU Texas p.67) are located but unread. ProcessWire asset paths (HSU) and PowerDMS (MSU Texas) are blocked or JavaScript-rendered. Governance behind SSO (Worcester State, UMGC faculty pages).
Protocol change: Status values: Found, Flag, Located not retrievable, Located behind login, Not reachable (recheck). Kirsti downloads the For Kirsti list. Absences from blocked sources are recorded as unverified, never as confirmed.

Finding: Formal policies (TXST AA/PPS 02.03.01 and 02.03.02, TSUS risk policy, TTU Reg. 09.04, UPR Cert. 66) say "artificial intelligence" and never "generative"; guidance pages say "generative AI" freely. A strict by-name test 3 excludes the formal policies and keeps the guidance.
Protocol change: Test 3 reworded to "addresses the use of AI tools by students, faculty, or staff," with the term recorded in AI term used.

Finding: AI language embedded as clauses inside general academic integrity policies (William Woods, UMGC 150.25, TXST Handbook, Missouri Valley) qualifies as a document, so the census will register AI governance at institutions where a standalone-document corpus recorded absence.
Protocol change: Field Standalone or embedded; three nested institution-level counts (any document, any standalone document, formal policy naming AI), each named whenever reported.

Finding: Two texts of the same code diverge: TXST UPPS 07.10.01 (no AI) vs Student Handbook rendering (AI clauses); Worcester State catalog Academic Honesty (no AI) vs IT portal restatement (AI clause); UMGC OAIA guidance public only on the library guide.
Protocol change: Each text is its own row, with the divergence in Notes and in Contradiction with another document.

Finding: Announced governance without a document: MSU Texas four-category framework (news release, task force due Mar 2027); UMGC institutional AI guidelines (press release Oct 2025, none public a year later); Morgan State Gemini license (IT news item only); Missouri Valley "Director of AI Innovation" title with no document.
Protocol change: Institution-level status "Announced, no document" with the announcement URL in Notes, and a field "AI role or body named without public document."

Finding: Requirement and template mismatch: UPR Cert. 66 Art. VII.B and TTU Reg. 09.04 mandate syllabus AI statements while the UPR Cert. 48 syllabus guide and RUM templates list no AI component; TXST AA/PPS 02.03.02 requires the statement while the Provost message "strongly encourages" it and the Honor Code Council hub says no policy exists.
Protocol change: Field Contradiction with another document (Y/N, with the paired row).

Finding: Null result at Henderson State coincides with no governance documentation updated since 2021 (2016 integrity policy, 2016 faculty handbook).
Protocol change: Institution-level status "No current public governance documentation" distinct from "No AI governance document located."

Finding: Dates were stated for roughly a third of documents; the rest rest on file paths or page metadata, and Gato CMS metadata records last publish (TXST cluster on 1 to 2 Oct 2026, a site refresh).
Protocol change: Field Date basis (stated, file path, page metadata, inferred, undated). Wave assignment inherits the basis.

Finding: Institution renamed since the 2025 Carnegie file (Missouri Valley College to University).
Protocol change: Field Operating name.

Finding: Morgan State is not a USM member (own Regents); MSU Texas is a TTU System member (Reg. 09.04 applies); Henderson State is ASU System (no AI policy) and must not be conflated with the University of Arkansas System (UASP 285.2, Apr 2026).
Protocol change: System affiliation and system AI policy become frame fields filled before the search.

Finding: The corpus record lists "Creighton memos (December 2025 and April 9, 2026), texastech.edu" as a primary source. The April 9 2026 memorandum (Course Content Guidelines) names no AI; the April 2026 TTU System AI document is Regulation 09.04. The December 2025 item appeared only in news coverage of AI-assisted course audits.
Protocol change: Kirsti to check the corpus row for the Creighton memos and decide whether it cites the memo (course content, AAUP context) or the regulation (AI).

Finding: Agents used 32 to 56 tool calls per institution, roughly 6 to 10 minutes wall clock each in parallel; Jackson State by hand took about 22 minutes. Yield 0 to 17 documents, median 2.
Protocol change: Planning estimate: 334 institutions at about 45 tool calls each, parallel batches of 10, about 35 batches. Verification load scales with documents found, roughly 2 per institution outside R1.

Finding: A section devoted to AI inside a larger document (handbook section, syllabus page section) raised the standalone question at William Woods and Jackson State.
Protocol change: An AI section inside a larger document is Embedded, even when titled as a policy. A document with its own page or catalog entry is Standalone.

Finding: Jackson State labels its common syllabus sections "University policies" with no separate policy instrument.
Protocol change: Where an institution names a text its policy, code type 3 on the institutional account.

Finding: Morgan State's governance minutes record a presentation without adopted position, and its license evidence appears only in press releases.
Protocol change: Minutes without an adopted position and press releases are boundary cases: recorded, counted as documents, flagged as boundary.

Finding: Robots-blocked and PDF-only sources (Henderson catalogs, William Woods handbooks, UPR certifications, Midwestern PowerDMS) yielded new documents once read in the browser with pdf.js; Henderson moved from 0 documents to 1.
Protocol change: Add a browser read of every catalog and handbook PDF before recording an absence.

Finding: A teaching center's workshop deck on writing syllabus AI policies (Jackson State, Jan 2026) advises instructors without stating an institutional rule.
Protocol change: Workshop materials from an institutional unit that advise instructors are type 5 Teaching guidance.
